title: Cap. VII: Ad alias rationes — Prima: ἐφ᾽ ᾧ as antecedent cause, not end
pass_a_gloss: Ad alias rationes quod spectat — utinam suus autor (sapientia+eloquentia) suscepisset tuendas; praestitisset multo melius quam ego. Prima sic se habet referente D. Garissolio (manuscriptum desumptarum non habeo; fidem penes eum). Nemo nescit: ἐφ᾽ ᾧ apud bonos autores vel finem rei (τὸ τέλος) vel causam antecedentem denotat — ut apud Synesium ἐφ᾽ ᾧ γεννάδιον ἔχαρε. Finis hic denotari non potest → causa antecedens designatur → vertatur eo quod / propterea quod. D. Gar respondet unum: ἐπί + relativum ὅς/ἥ/ὅ aliquando finem aliquando causam notat, sed frequentissime vim praepositionis ἐν (Marc. 2.4 ἐφ᾽ ᾧ κατέκειτο in quo jacebat). Placeus: aberratio ab argumento — agebatur de ἐφ᾽ ᾧ absolute positis (absque expresso antecedente ad ᾧ). Ubi proximum antecedens adest, quis unquam vertit eo quod/propterea quod? Hic absolute: proxime antecedit θάνατος bis + ante illud ἁμαρτία; ad neutrum referri constat. Praecedit Genitivus ἀνθρώπου; sed interjecta nomina immo commata obstunt quominus ad eum referatur.
pass_b_english: As for the other reasons, would that their own author had undertaken to defend them — by the wisdom and eloquence with which he seems to me to be marked — he would have performed that far better than I. The first stands thus, as D. Garissoles reports it; for I do not have the manuscript from which they were taken. Faith must rest with him. Nobody is ignorant that ἐφ᾽ ᾧ, among good authors, either denotes the end of a thing (τὸ τέλος) or an antecedent cause, as in Synesius, ἐφ᾽ ᾧ γεννάδιον ἔχαρε. Since therefore an end cannot be denoted in this place, it follows that an antecedent cause is designated, and that it be rendered "in that," or "because." What does D. Garissoles answer? This one thing only: that ἐπί joined with the relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, although it sometimes marks an end and sometimes an antecedent cause, nevertheless most frequently has the force of the preposition ἐν. Mark 2:4: ἐφ᾽ ᾧ κατέκειτο, "in which he was lying," and so on. But what is this except a wandering from the argument? For in the argument the discussion was of the words ἐφ᾽ ᾧ placed absolutely — that is, without an expressed antecedent to which the pronoun ᾧ is referred. For when there is a near antecedent to which it is referred, who ever thought those words ought to be rendered "in that" or "because"? But here they are placed absolutely: for what immediately precedes is the noun θάνατος used twice, and before that ἁμαρτία; and it is established that they are referred to neither neuter. The genitive ἀνθρώπου, "man," does indeed precede; but intervening nouns — nay, even commas — stand in the way of referring the relative to him (Romans 5:12).
source_text: Ad alias rationes quod spectat, utinam eas suus autor suscepisset tuendas, qua mihi videtur esse et sapientia et eloquentia, praestitisset id, quam ego, multo melius. Prima sic se habet, referente D. Garissolio; Manuscriptum enim ex quo sunt desumptae non habeo. Fidem esse penes eum oportet. Nemo nescit illud, ἐφ᾽ ᾧ, apud bonos autores, vel denotare finem rei, τὸ τέλος, vel causam antecedentem, ut apud Synesium, ἐφ᾽ ᾧ γεννάδιον ἔχαρε. Cum igitur finis hoc loco denotari non possit, sequitur ut causa antecedens designetur, et vertatur eo quod, vel propterea quod. Quid respondet D. Gar? Hoc unum, ἐπί junctum cum relativo ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, quanquam aliquando finem, aliquando causam antecedentem notet, tamen frequentissime vim habere praepositionis ἐν. Marc. 2. 4. ἐφ᾽ ᾧ κατέκειτο in quo jacebat &c. Sed quid hoc est, nisi aberratio ab argumento? Nam in argumento agebatur de vocibus ἐφ᾽ ᾧ absolute positis, hoc est, absque expresso antecedente ad quod pronomen ᾧ referatur. Cum enim est in proximo antecedens ad quod refertur, quis unquam eas vertendas putavit eo quod vel propterea quod? Hic autem ponuntur absolute, quod enim proxime antecedit est nomen θάνατος bis usurpatum, ac ante illud ἁμαρτία; ad neutrum referri constat. Praecedit quidem Genitivus ἀνθρώπου hominem; Sed quominus ad eum referri possit, obstant interjecta nomina, immo commata.
